keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Awsan (its Hadhramaut and Sabaean shapes begin later and elsewhere). The page gives no area: the capital city is 15 hectares with irrigation over about 6,800 hectares, and the Wadi Markha core is 'archaeologically unexplored'. The shape is the region name 'Awsan', which the gazetteer lacks; the sabaeans, qataban and hadhramaut dossiers use the same name. A gazetteer entry would be the Wadi Markha basin, a few thousand km2 around Hajar Yahirr in Shabwah Governorate.

ledger.note: 8th century BC: Awsan arises at Wadi Markha. Infobox 'Established: 8th century BC'; 'The first began in the 8th century BC' (the first of two kingdoms of the name), allied with Saba. A century is not a year; mid-century is a convention.

ledger.note: late 7th century BC: Saba destroys Awsan. 'In the late 7th century BC, this alliance changed into a rivalry'; 'the Kingdom of Awsan was destroyed by Saba and its allies', its king Murattaa defeated (the Sabaean claim: 16,000 killed and 40,000 captured). The Karib'il Watar page has him 'continued his advance to reach the lands of Awsan' and 'burn all their cities all the way to the sea' (undated; the page dates him both 'fl. late 7th century' and 'early 7th century'). 625 is the middle of the late 7th century.

notes: Cliopatria has no Awsan. The name 'Awsan' as a region is absent from the gazetteer (the sabaeans, qataban and hadhramaut dossiers use {"region": "Awsan"} too); the gazetteer agent should define it as the Wadi Markha basin in Shabwah Governorate. The Awsan page describes a second kingdom: 'The later kingdom of Awsan experienced a resurgence around or after the 2nd century BC' (Robin: 2nd century BC; Schiettecatte: 1st century BC), later regaining control under Qataban's declining influence, and a 2nd-century AD Sabaean inscription mentioning war against Awsan; no extent or end is dated, so it is not drawn here (a gap-filler could add a second dossier or an extension). The page is inconsistent on the destruction's date only in wording ('late 7th century BC' against Karib'il Watar 'early 7th'); the sabaeans dossier has Hadhramaut a Sabaean vassal from 675 (bridged) and the destruction of Awsan in 625, the year used here.
